headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Dealing with Leaky Faucets
articleBody: When your faucet starts leaking, it’s natural to want to fix it fast, but sometimes our well-intentioned efforts can lead to bigger problems. Here are a few common mistakes we see people make that you should definitely avoid. First, don't ignore it, even if it's just a tiny drip. Small leaks waste water and can cause significant damage over time to your fixtures and even your cabinetry. Second, resist the urge to overtighten everything. This often damages components and can strip threads, making the repair much more complicated and costly. Third, don't assume all faucets are the same. Different types (compression, cartridge, ceramic disc, ball) require specific repair methods and parts. Using the wrong approach can break things further. Fourth, using incorrect replacement parts is a big no-no; generic parts might fit, but they often don't last, leading to another leak sooner than you'd like. Finally, don't wait too long to call a professional if you're unsure. While some leaks are simple DIY fixes, many require an expert touch to ensure the job is done right and lasts.
